_skill.name: sub_label_annotation
_skill.description: LLM-facing label catalog (main, sub, segment_type only). Per-label description, hierarchy (parent/children), exclusive_with constraints, annotation_guideline, and search_tags. Descriptions and search_tags carry inline VLM / deterministic preflight predicates so hybrid (vector + BM25) similarity over observation text shortlists the matching labels. Circuit and circuit_section labels are NOT in this catalog — the LLM picks them via the `get_circuit_id` / `locate_circuit_section` tools (geometry from app/shared/circuit_sections.py), not by search.
when_to_use: Drilling into a parent-labelled section to pick sub-labels (detailed flow).
Hybrid-similarity shortlist of candidate labels from VLM observations.
Validating label hierarchy (parent presence, mutual exclusion).

range_fit_rule: Whole-range label rule for detailed annotation: every proposed label must describe the proposed child range as a whole. Do not propose a label because it matches only one phase, one apex moment, or a short slice inside the child range; shrink the child range so the label fits throughout, submit a separate proposal for the smaller range, or omit that label.

O.name: Successful Overtake
O.description: Player gained a position on a specific opponent inside the section. Required gate: `classify_opponent_interaction(start, end)` must return `outcome: pass_completed`, `gates.O: true`, and `label_gates.O: true`. Low / weak confidence requires opponent-trajectory inspection or omitting the label. The classifier's primary slot is the opponent to cite. A close opponent with `outcome: failed_attack` is MSR, not O. Defensive holds are OD; failed defenses are MSR.
O.annotation_guideline:
How to identify the sublabels for Successful Overtake: Step 1 — Confirm the pass. Call `classify_opponent_interaction(start, end)`. The result MUST have `outcome: pass_completed`, `gates.O: true`, and `label_gates.O: true`. If not, do NOT propose any O sub-label — use the classifier outcome to decide OD, MSR, or no-O. Quote `primary_slot_for_role`, `outcome`, `confidence`, `confidence_level`, `entry_signed_long_gap_m`, `exit_signed_long_gap_m`, `min_distance_m`, `min_lateral_offset_m`, and `side_by_side_iloc_count` from the classifier / nearest-opponent evidence. Step 2 — Pick the technique sub-label by where the pass happened and how the player's own trace diverges from the expert:
  - O1 (late-brake attack at corner entry): player's brake
    initiation later than expert + tightening trajectory.
  - O3 (outside-line sweep through a corner): trajectory wider
    than expert through entry-to-apex.
  - O4 (switchback): offset crosses outside-at-entry to
    inside-at-exit, earlier throttle on exit.
  - O5 (slipstream on a straight): speed > expert with throttle
    ≤ expert; gap closed smoothly. Confirm with
    `query_opponent_trajectory(start, end, slot, n_samples)`.
O.search_tags: O; Successful Overtake; type main; successful overtake; opponent interaction; pass completed

OD.name: Successful Defense
OD.description: Player held position against a real, close opponent inside the section. Required gate: `classify_opponent_interaction(start, end)` must return `outcome: held_defense`, `gates.OD: true`, and `label_gates.OD: true`. Low / weak confidence requires opponent-trajectory inspection or omitting the label. A merely close opponent with no held-defense outcome is not OD; a player who lost the position is MSR (`broken_defense`), not OD.
OD.annotation_guideline:
How to identify the sublabels for Successful Defense: Step 1 — Confirm the defense. Call `classify_opponent_interaction(start, end)`. Require `outcome: held_defense`, `gates.OD: true`, and `label_gates.OD: true`. If the classifier does not return held defense with enough confidence, the section is not OD. Quote the same classifier / opponent fields as for O in reasoning. Step 2 — Pick the technique sub-label by where the defense happened:
  - OD1 (inside cover at corner entry): player's brake
    initiation earlier than expert and/or trajectory tighter
    than expert through entry-to-apex; opponent close on the
    outside / behind.
  - OD2 (defensive lift on a straight): player's throttle drops
    below expert with no matching brake; opponent close behind,
    gap shrinks during the lift without flipping past the
    player. Confirm with `query_opponent_trajectory`.
OD.search_tags: OD; Successful Defense; type main; successful defense; opponent interaction; held defense

EA.name: Expert Adherence (Training)
EA.description: Driver closely follows or cleanly outperforms the expert's line and speed profile.  Look for **overall gap holds stable**, **gap shrinks**, or player-ahead evidence in the time delta when available, plus **speed match** or better speed with no instability.  The player's **entry trajectory** and **exit trajectory** usually track the expert with trajectory offset **aligned** (within ±0.5 m of zero), but EA can still apply to a cleaner/faster line that is wider or tighter than the expert when there is no off-track/cutting/instability evidence and no MSP/RM/MSR/PS gate.
EA.annotation_guideline: How to identify the sublabels for Expert Adherence (Training): The driver is following or cleanly outperforming the optimal racing line and speed profile closely.  Nothing needs to be labeled right now.
EA.search_tags: EA; Expert Adherence (Training); type main; entry; exit

PS.name: Pit Stop
PS.description: Driver entering, waiting in, or exiting the pit lane. Require available pit evidence: `Graphics_is_in_pit` or position evidence that the segment overlaps the circuit's known pit entry, pit lane, or pit-exit corridor. Do not label PS from dramatic speed reduction, trajectory deviation, or acceleration back toward track speed alone.
PS.annotation_guideline: How to identify the sublabels for Pit Stop: The driver is entering, waiting in, or exiting the pit lane. Use PS for pit-lane procedure, not RM. First verify `Graphics_is_in_pit` or compatible pit-entry/pit-lane/pit-exit position. Add PS1 when the segment is specifically pit exit: the position is compatible with pit exit and the car accelerates back toward track speed after leaving the pit lane.
PS.search_tags: PS; Pit Stop; type main; pit stop; pit exit; entry; exit

RM.name: Recovery & Merge
RM.description: Driver recovering from a prior mistake and merging back to the racing line. The trajectory offset shows **recovery** toward the expert line, with speed/throttle consistent with rejoining or accelerating back toward pace. Time delta may show **gap shrinks**, or may still show **gap grows** while `slope_shape` shows recovery shape. Do not use RM for normal pit exit; pit exit is PS / PS1.
RM.annotation_guideline: How to identify sublabels for Recovery & Merge: The driver is recovering from a mistake. Step 1: Analyze the 'Time Difference to Expert' graph with `compute_slope`; use its deterministic unit and trend-significance fields. A significant falling `total_change_direction` is strong RM evidence, but a significant rising total change can still be RM when `slope_shape` shows recovery shape and the action evidence shows recovery / merge rather than a new technical mistake. Tiny ms changes are not RM evidence. Step 2: Examine the 'trajectory_offset' graph to identify recovery - look for the offset trending back toward zero from either side after a prior mistake/off-track, using query near-zero/toward-zero fields when available. Step 3: Examine the 'speed_delta' graph to identify if the player is accelerating back toward the expert's speed profile. Step 4: use the 'compute_expert_phases' tool (it produces a 'phase_indices' attachment contains the indices for entry/apex/exit). Do not label pit exit as RM unless it follows a separate driving mistake that requires recovery.
RM.search_tags: RM; Recovery & Merge; type main; recovery; merge; moves toward zero; recovery toward expert line; pit exit; exit

MSP.name: Mistake (Practice)
MSP.description: Technical driving error causing time loss or vehicle instability, NOT caused by interaction with a close opponent. Time delta shows **gap grows** and the trajectory offset shows a clear deviation from the expert's line (offset **wider than expert** or **tighter than expert**) that does not recover inside the range. If the dominant action is merge/rejoin recovery back toward the expert line, use RM instead even when the absolute time gap is still growing. When `classify_opponent_interaction` returns an adverse racing outcome (`failed_attack` or `broken_defense`), the section is MSR, not MSP.
MSP.annotation_guideline: How to identify sublabels for Practice Mistake: The driver has committed a technical driving error. Step 1: Analyze the 'Time Difference to Expert' graph with `compute_slope`; require `total_change_direction: "rising"` and `total_change_is_label_significant: true` for time-loss evidence, and cite `slope_shape` when the loss-rate slope changes over the section. Do not describe tiny positive ms changes as strong. Do not use MSP when the trajectory is moving back toward zero and speed/throttle show a merge or rejoin recovery; that is RM even if the time gap still grows overall. Step 2: Examine the differences in 'throttle' between the player and the expert to identify when the driver applied too much or too little throttle, or got on/off the throttle at the wrong time. Step 3: Examine the differences in 'brake' between the player and the expert to identify if the driver braked too hard or too softly, or got on/off the brake at the wrong time. Step 4: Examine the 'trajectory_balance' graph to find understeer (blue / front-slip dominant) or oversteer (red / rear-slip dominant), which could lead to lower speed. Step 5: For entry/apex/exit shape questions, request the 'trajectory_offset' graph and include the 'compute_expert_phases' tool on the same step (it produces a 'phase_indices' attachment contains the phase indices for entry/apex/exit). Step 6: Before committing in opponent-capable data, call `classify_opponent_interaction(start, end)` — if it returns `failed_attack` or `broken_defense`, the section is MSR, not MSP.
MSP.search_tags: MSP; Mistake (Practice); type main; technical mistake; gap grows; time loss; sub-label calculation; wider than expert; tighter than expert

MSR.name: Mistake (Racing)
MSR.description: Time / position loss caused by an interaction with a close opponent. Required gate: `classify_opponent_interaction(start, end)` returns `outcome: failed_attack` or `outcome: broken_defense` with `gates.MSR: true` and `label_gates.MSR: true`. Low / weak confidence requires opponent-trajectory inspection or omitting the label. If the classifier does not support an adverse racing outcome, this is not MSR.
MSR.annotation_guideline:
How to identify sublabels for Racing Mistake: Step 1 — Confirm the adverse racing outcome. Call `classify_opponent_interaction(start, end)`. Require `outcome: failed_attack` or `outcome: broken_defense`, `gates.MSR: true`, and `label_gates.MSR: true`. If not, the section is not MSR. Step 2 — Pick the outcome family from the classifier:
  - Failed overtake attempt: `outcome: failed_attack` — the player attacked but the pass did not complete.
  - Defense broken: `outcome: broken_defense` — the opponent got through by exit.
Step 3 — Pick the specific subtype by the player's trace. The MSR subtypes mirror the O / OD subtypes (same telemetry shape, opposite outcome). Prefer a specific subtype over the generic label when the trace lets you identify the attempt type:
  - MSR3 (failed O1 late-brake attack at entry): brake
    **initiation onset later than** expert + entry trajectory
    tightening, but no pass.
  - MSR4 (failed O3 outside-line sweep): trajectory **wider
    than expert** through entry-to-apex, but no pass.
  - MSR5 (failed O4 switchback): offset crosses outside-at-entry
    to inside-at-exit (or the reverse intent), but no pass.
  - MSR6 (failed O5 slipstream gain): on a straight, speed >
    expert with throttle ≤ expert, gap closes but doesn't flip.
  - MSR7 (broken OD1 inside cover): brake earlier than expert
    and/or trajectory tighter, but opponent got through.
  - MSR8 (broken OD2 defensive lift): throttle drops below
    expert on a straight, but opponent got through.
  - MSR1 / MSR2: only when the attempt-type signature cannot
    be identified from the trace.
MSR.search_tags: MSR; Mistake (Racing); type main; racing mistake; opponent interaction; failed attack; broken defense

RM1.name: Recover from off-track
RM1.description: Driver returning to track after an off-track excursion — the trajectory offset peaks far **wider than expert** earlier in the segment (a prior **moving toward positive (widening)** beat), then shows **recovery** (offset trending back toward zero) while the speed trace shows the driver rejoining or accelerating back toward pace. Time delta may show **gap shrinks**, or a still-rising gap whose `slope_shape` shows recovery shape.
RM1.search_tags: RM1; Recover from off-track; type sub; parent RM; recovery; merge; moves toward zero; recovery toward expert line; wider than expert; moving toward positive

PS1.name: Exit pit lane
PS1.description: Driver re-joining the track after a pit stop - the segment position overlaps the circuit's pit-exit corridor, the speed trace rises from low pit-exit speed (an **acceleration onset** well below normal corner-exit speed), `Graphics_is_in_pit` clears when available, and the car follows the pit-exit path back toward track speed. This is pit procedure, not recovery from a mistake. Do not infer PS1 from low speed plus wide trajectory alone when the position is a normal racing section away from pit exit.

category_guidelines.Segment Type: Use one base segment-shape label when clear: ST1 In the corner, ST2 On the straight, ST3 Approach to corner, ST4 Exit corner leading to straight, ST5 Between consecutive corners, or ST6 Consecutive corners with no straight in between. ST3 means the range starts before the detected corner arc and ends before the apex; do not use ST3 for a range that includes the apex or corner exit. ST4 means the exit section of the corner itself as it leads toward a straight; it does not mean a range that includes the completed corner plus a substantial portion of the following straight. For corner segments, optionally add one corner-shape refinement when clear: ST7 Constant-radius corner, ST8 Increasing-radius corner, ST9 Decreasing-radius corner, ST10 Hairpin corner, or ST11 Chicane or esses. Add a corner-shape refinement only when `measure_segment_shape.corner_shape_refinement.shape_key` matches that label's `deterministic_gate.required_shape_key` for the final range; non-empty `phases` alone is not enough. ST10 requires `measure_segment_shape.corner_shape_refinement` to report the required hairpin gate flag true: `is_near_u_turn`. Entry/apex/exit altitude labels (ST12-ST20) are phase-specific subsegment labels. Do not attach them to a lap parent segment that covers the whole corner; use them only when the annotation range is the matching corner phase subsegment.
